goal: A red that only a loaded machine produces is measured again, not blamed on the pull request. memoro-cli's own tests assert order and overlap, not wall-clock windows, and no test reads the machine's live gate lock.

Seen 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-12. #891 (a role text and a changelog fragment) went red on `tests/mc/repo-status.test.js`, `repo-watch.test.js` and `work-resume.test.js` right after a deploy; the same files passed 32/32 alone and 1636/1636 in the round's own 74-file selection. #872 (docs only) went red on a 300 ms window in `merger.test.js` and an ordering test in `repo-gate.test.js`. memoro #13470 had all 19 tests of `build-bundle.test.js` cancelled when their `before` hook ran past 10 minutes at load ~38. Each time the round said "the red files pass on the base — this change broke them" from one quiet re-run of the base, and a mend session was spent finding nothing to fix. `tests/mc/page.test.js` is red whenever a real merge round holds a gate lock on the machine (three proposals, 2026-10-10 and 2026-10-11).
contract: No pull request lands on a weaker measurement than today's. A red that passes alone is measured again in a full round; it is never counted green, and a second red round is answered red as today.
A test keeps asserting what it asserts today (overlap, order, an answer within a bound); only a wall-clock margin that load can eat goes.
Every step runs `npm test` and lands through `mc merge memoro-cli <pr>`. A change to the merger takes effect when the merger next starts.
out_of_scope: memoro's own load-sensitive tests (`pdf-sandbox-timeout.test.js`, `docx-sandbox-timeout.test.js`, `build-bundle.test.js`): their fixes are memoro pull requests. This plan only stops the merger from blaming the change for them.
Whole-repository scanners the local `mc gate` selection did not reach (one-window-path step 8, `css-dead-rules.test.js`): a separate question.
Lane caps, the selector, and the step lifecycle faults Martin fixes outside the runner on 2026-10-12 (blocked-step PRs, foreign PRs booked on a step, stacked close-outs, derived SDK artifacts).

success_criteria.criterion: A round whose red files pass on the base is not answered "this change broke them" until the same files have also been run alone on the candidate and stayed red there. Red files that pass alone on both, and a file whose tests were cancelled with none failed, stop the round as `red-under-load`, which the merger measures again once, as it does `file-killed`.
success_criteria.check: `tests/mc/repo-gate.test.js` and `tests/mc/merger.test.js` on fake tests: red in the round, green alone on base and head → `red-under-load` and a second round; red alone on the head → today's red and wording; cancelled > 0 with fail 0 → `red-under-load`; a second `red-under-load` → answered red with the reason naming both quiet passes. Live: the close-out quotes a merger.log `measuring again` line for a `red-under-load`, or says none occurred.

success_criteria.criterion: memoro-cli's timing tests assert order and overlap, not a wall-clock window: `child-async.test.js` "two children started together run side by side", `merger.test.js` around the 300 ms light-job window (~line 931), `repo-gate.test.js` "starts the gates with the suite…", `repo-status.test.js` "one repository by name…", `repo-watch.test.js` "within three rounds…", `work-resume.test.js` "it is the resume that is refused…".
success_criteria.check: Each of those files run 10 times in a row while a full `npm test` runs beside it in another shell: 10/10 green. The tests still fail on the fault they guard (shown by breaking the code under test once, in the PR body).

success_criteria.criterion: No test in `tests/mc/` reads the machine's real gate lock or mc home: `collectPage` reaches `runningMerges` with the root its `env` names.
success_criteria.check: `tests/mc/page.test.js` "builds every section from the files…" passes while a fake gate lock is written under the real `mcHome()` by the test itself (and removed after); `npm test` is green.

steps.title: 1. A red that passes alone on the base and the head is measured again
steps.done_when: In a red round, after `probeMainRed` (`src/mc/selector-miss.js`) finds the red files green on the base, the round runs the same files alone on the candidate head; green there too stops the round `red-under-load`. A file whose TAP totals show cancelled > 0 and fail 0 is `red-under-load` without any re-run. The merger measures a `red-under-load` once more like `file-killed` (`src/mc/merger.js` ~491); a second one is answered red with a reason that says the files passed alone on base and head. Tests per the first criterion; `npm test` is green.
instruction: Today `repo-gate.js` (~660–700) answers a red round, then `probeMain` re-runs the red files on the base. When they pass there, `selector-miss.js:86` says `the red files pass on the base — this change broke them` and the round is the change's red. That is one sample on a quieter machine: on 2026-10-12 #891 (text only) and on 2026-10-11 #872 (docs only) were blamed this way, and both went green unchanged.

**The head re-run.** When `probeMain` returns with no `red_on_main` and the round has `red_files`, run those files alone on the candidate head in `headDir` with the round's own `runTests` and `flags` (the same call `redAt` makes on the base). Any file still red there: the round is red as today, and the line says `red alone on the candidate too — this change broke them`. None red: `finish('red-under-load', '<files> red in the round, green alone on the base and on the candidate — measured again')`, with `report.under_load_files` listing them. Only the files that were red are run, so this costs seconds on a round that has already failed.

**Cancelled is not failed.** `tap-red.js` already reads `cancelled`. A red file whose totals are cancelled > 0 and fail 0 (a `before` hook that timed out, as memoro's `build-bundle.test.js` on #13470) is under load, not the change's: treat it as a file that passed alone, without re-running it. A file with fail > 0 stays red whatever else it has.

**The merger.** Beside `file-killed` at `merger.js` ~491, a `red-under-load` round is measured again once (`underLoadOnce`, the same shape as `killedOnce`), with the line `<files> red only under load — measuring again`. A second `red-under-load` for the same job is answered red with its reason, so the step's next session reads that the files pass alone and the round twice did not. `merge-step.js` ~124 lists the stops that do not count as the step's red: add `red-under-load` beside `file-killed` only for the first one.
**Docs.** `docs/technical/mc-merge.md`: one paragraph beside `file-killed` naming `red-under-load`, the head re-run and the cancelled rule. A `changelog.d/` fragment.

**Tests.** In `tests/mc/repo-gate.test.js` and `tests/mc/merger.test.js`, with the fakes those files already use for the main-red probe and `file-killed`: the four cases in the first criterion's check. Archive the proposals this step answers by moving them to `~/mc/proposals/archive/`: `2026-10-12-load-flaky-repo-status-watch-resume.md`, `2026-10-11-merger-timing-tests-flake-under-load.md`, `2026-10-11-build-bundle-timeout-under-load.md` and `2026-10-10-sandbox-timeout-tests-flake-under-load.md` (the last two keep their memoro half: say so in the PR body).

steps.title: 2. memoro-cli's timing tests assert order, not milliseconds
steps.done_when: The six tests named in the second criterion assert overlap, order or an answer within a bound measured against the test's own serial baseline, with no fixed wall-clock margin under one second; each file passes 10 of 10 runs beside a full `npm test`; `npm test` is green.
instruction: Read each test before changing it, and say in the PR body what it guards and how the new assertion still catches that fault. Known so far: `tests/mc/child-async.test.js:54` asserts two 200 ms `sleep` children finish in < 350 ms (failed at 365 ms in a full gate on 2026-10-10); what it guards is overlap, so compare against one child's measured time (both together take less than 1.5 × one child plus the spawn cost measured in the same test), or lengthen the children so the margin is seconds. `tests/mc/merger.test.js` ~931 already names a 300 ms window that ran out on a loaded machine: replace the window with an event the test awaits (the light job answered before the heavy round is released). `tests/mc/repo-gate.test.js:1250` asserts start order and awaiting: assert the order of recorded events, not their timing.

`tests/mc/repo-status.test.js:177`, `tests/mc/repo-watch.test.js:176` and `tests/mc/work-resume.test.js:184` are synchronous tests that went red together on 2026-10-12 right after a deploy and passed alone. Find what they share that load or a deploy can move: a `spawnSync` timeout, a real process, a file under the real home, or a clock read. Fix that cause, not the assertion. If it is a path outside the test's temporary root, it belongs with step 3's fix and is fixed here the same way.

**Measure.** For each changed file: `for i in $(seq 10); do node --test --import ./tests/_isolate-home.mjs <file> || echo RED; done` while `npm test` runs in a second shell; quote the counts in the PR body. Break the code under test once per file (locally, not committed) and quote the red, so the test is shown to still guard something.

steps.title: 3. No test reads the machine's live gate lock
steps.done_when: `collectPage` (`src/mc/page-collect.js`) passes the work root its `env` resolves to `runningMerges` (`src/mc/merges-collect.js:39`), so `root` no longer defaults to the real `mcHome()` there; `tests/mc/page.test.js` "builds every section from the files…" passes with a fake lock written under the real `mcHome()` during the test; no other `tests/mc/` file reads the real mc home (checked as in the instruction); `npm test` is green.
instruction: `tests/mc/page.test.js:1994` passes `env: { MC_WORK_ROOT: root }`, but the MERGES reading goes through `runningMerges`, whose `root` defaults to `mcHome()`, the real one. While a real round holds a lock (2026-10-10 #13390, 2026-10-11 #13467) the test reads it as `data.merges.landing` and fails at the `assert.equal(data.merges.landing, null)` near line 2026. Find where `collectPage` calls `merges(...)` and give it the root that `env` names, the way the other readings in `collectPage` already get theirs; if `mcHome` itself takes an env, use that.

**The test.** In the test itself, write a gate-lock file shaped as `runningRounds` reads it under the real `mcHome()` for the duration of the test (a unique slug, removed in `after`), and assert the page still reads no landing. That is the case the three proposals saw, made deterministic.

**The sweep.** `grep -rn "mcHome()" src/mc` for every default that falls back to the real home, and check that each reader the page tests reach is handed the test's root. Name what you checked in the PR body; fix any other reader the same way.

steps.title: 4. The close
steps.done_when: Every criterion is `met` with its check quoted; steps 1–3 are `done` with their PRs; `docs/project/project_log.md` has the project's row; the merger has restarted on the new code and the close-out quotes merger.log for a `red-under-load` or says none has occurred since; `npm test` is green.
instruction: Run each criterion's check on `main` after steps 1–3 have landed and set `met` only on what the check shows. For the first criterion's live half, read `~/mc/runner/log/merger.log` since step 1 landed for `red only under load` and quote it, or write that none occurred.
Add the row to `docs/project/project_log.md` the way the rows above it read, and make sure every proposal named in steps 1–3 is under `~/mc/proposals/archive/`.
